target_customer: Consumers who want strength training at home, paying for hardware plus a monthly membership
problem: Home workouts lack form feedback and real trainers; gym visits cost time and money.
business_model: Hardware (home gym, smart weights) plus monthly membership for live and virtual training
product_category: Connected home fitness with computer vision

founders.name: Moawia Eldeeb
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a Columbia graduate passionate about AI, fitness and consumer startups.

founders.name: Joshua Augustin
founders.background_notes: Named Founder/CTO on the YC page; TechCrunch (2021-04-13) names him as co-founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: The product needs 3D sensors, computer vision and machine learning to count reps and track form, plus hardware manufacturing and supply chain. Reviews and VentureBeat (2019-07-18) describe sensors and ML for rep counting and form.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus content subscription creates switching costs, but VentureBeat and later reviews name Peloton and Tonal as rivals with deep funding, and connected fitness was a crowded category by 2020.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Peloton and Tonal were named as competitors in 2019 coverage and later reviews. Tempo was not acquired; a Fitt Insider roundup mentions a 10 percent layoff at Tempo, year unclear.

market_need_then: Connected home fitness demand surged in 2020 and 2021; TechCrunch (2021-04-13) quotes the CEO saying investors approached Tempo and sales rose tenfold in the prior year per Front Office Sports.

branding.domain_note: Uses tempo.fit; the exact tempo.com is not used.

identity.visual_style: Color-coded smart weights shown on the site

branding.brand_signature: Color-coded smart weights with live form feedback

rebrands.why: Not stated. A directory says the company was formerly Pivot Interactive and MobiHealthNews covered Pivot in 2019 under the same founder; date of rename not found.

branding.community_and_virality: Official Facebook group with over 9.7k members per tempo.fit; Gizmodo and TechCrunch covered the Tempo Move launch in 2021-11.

brand_strength.rationale: Large press coverage and product reviews, an owner community, but the Tempo name is shared with many unrelated companies and no source ties growth to the brand.

outcome_analysis: Tempo started in YC Winter 2015 and stayed quiet until a 17 million dollar Series A in July 2019 under the name Pivot. It then raised 60 million dollars in July 2020 and 220 million dollars in April 2021 as home fitness demand surged, bringing total funding to nearly 300 million. Later press mentions a layoff of 10 percent and the company remains independent and active, so its long-term outcome is unresolved.
notes: Founded year: YC says 2014 while TechCrunch calls the company five years old in 2021 and a directory says 2015. Seed of about 1.8M dollars from Khosla, SignalFire and Y Combinator appears only in a funding database, so it is not recorded as a round. Series A date: VentureBeat is dated 2019-07-18 while a Crunchbase-derived result says Feb 2020. Series C lead is reported as SoftBank Vision Fund or Vision Fund 2. The Series B 250M valuation is a Bloomberg report. The YC page text mentions SmartSpot and raising over 300M, which conflicts with 220M reported. Competitors: Peloton and Tonal appear only in 2019 and later coverage, so none are listed for 2015.
